  - Empty or omitted: disable affinity

HeaderName: request and response header carrying the affinity ID
  - Default when Mode is enabled: X-Tencent-Agr-Affinity-Id
  - Constraint: a non-reserved HTTP field name of 1-128 ASCII bytes; omit when affinity is disabled

Flags.Description: StorageMounts as a JSON array, @file, or - for stdin. Omit --storage-mounts or pass [] to keep the current mounts. Match an existing Image volume by Name and omit MountPath and ReadOnly.
Flags.Name: storage-mounts
Values: Name: name of an existing Image volume on the tool
Reference: image reference with a tag or sha256 digest
ImageRegistryType: personal or enterprise; required with Image
SubPath: omitted keeps the current directory, an empty string switches to the image root, a non-empty string switches to that directory
With --request, you can reuse an Image mount from tool get. AGR strips MountPath and ReadOnly to preserve the tool's settings.
The update response acknowledges the request. --wait checks the tool lifecycle (ACTIVE or ISOLATED).

Read back the named mount before starting an instance.
  agr tool get sdt-example -o json --jq '.Data.StorageMounts[]? | select(.Name == "runtime") | .StorageSource.Image'

Repeat readback until Reference and ImageRegistryType match and the expected SubPath is visible. An omitted SubPath in the request keeps the previous directory. For an explicit empty SubPath, an empty or omitted readback means the image root.
When reusing a tag, confirm Digest matches the expected digest from your registry before starting an instance. The other fields can match while the previous image is still mounted.
To select an immutable image, use a digest-pinned Reference such as <registry>/<image>@sha256:<digest>.

Endpoint.Description: HTTP/WebSocket destination without user information, query or fragment.

ExitCode.Description: Observed local subprocess exit code. Remote program exits remain business results.

Field.Description: Configuration or request field name, never its value.

HTTPStatus.Description: Observed HTTP response status; absent when no response was received or the SDK does not expose it. Mobile handshake HTTP 401/403 uses TUNNEL_AUTH_FAILED. Proxy metadata appears in diagnostics, not a CLI response envelope.

InstanceId.Description: Sandbox instance involved in a failed remote connection or invocation.

LogPath.Description: Tunnel log path on startup failure, only when the log file was successfully created.

Operation.Description: Observed operation or API action, without command arguments or payloads.

Path.Description: Necessary local file path, or stdin/stdout for stream input/output.

Program.Description: Local subprocess executable; arguments and environment are omitted.

RequestId.Description: Server request identifier when available. HTTP/WebSocket response headers accept X-TC-RequestId, then X-Request-Id; only nonempty printable ASCII values without spaces, at most 256 bytes, are retained. Other response headers and bodies are omitted.

Stage.Description: Observed boundary, such as http_request, websocket_handshake, subprocess_start, subprocess_exit, config_read, config_parse, config_decode, config_validate, request_input, request_parse, local_file, file_transfer, remote_connect, remote_execute, local_terminal, remote_start, remote_ready or remote_stream. Tunnel readiness retains start, exit, readiness_protocol and readiness_wait. Proxy logs use http_request, http_response and ws_handshake. No inferred DNS/TCP/TLS stage.

TimeoutMs.Description: Known request, WebSocket handshake or readiness budget in milliseconds, captured before the operation (not elapsed time). Omitted when no budget is available.
